correction.retracted: 'no world model adds skill' (from the generated-fit rescore write-up)
correction.why_wrong: that read global macro AUC, which pools all (root,action) pairs. Safe-action choice is a ranking WITHIN a root over its 17 forks. The two disagree.
correction.evidence: Direct-Mamba selection .917 vs its own root+action control .611, paired cluster bootstrap +.306 CI [+.125,+.487], excludes zero - while its death AUC (.782) sits on that control (.787).

ORACLE_decomposition.what: safe-action selection using the REAL observed successor encodings and a probe fitted on real successors. No world model is involved: this is the ceiling the representation permits.
ORACLE_decomposition.reading: Direct picks the safe fork EVERY time from real successors; every LeWM arm is BELOW the .611 action-only floor. Global death AUC differs by only .056 (.749 vs .805) while within-root selection differs by .611 (.389 vs 1.000). The deficit is in the REPRESENTATION, not the dynamics, and global AUC is nearly blind to it.

action_conditioning.what: mean pairwise distance between the 17 successor branches, over latent norm
action_conditioning.reading: mamba_raw reproduces the true action-spread almost exactly (.977) and still selects at the floor, so fidelity of action-conditioning is not the limit. mamba_tc has the LARGEST observed spread (.435) and the WORST oracle (.222): the branches differ, but along directions unrelated to death. transformer_tc barely responds to actions at all (.189), which explains its degeneracy separately.

structural_confound.note: Direct differs on width, spatial structure AND context at once. Only the sequence mixer was ever varied inside the LeWM line (Mamba -> Transformer at 4.92x params: no change), so the confound between pooling, width, context and objective has never been broken.
